protocol: Extend the abdominal examination to the lung bases, pleura, pericardium (subxiphoid window) and the chest wall at the site of maximal tenderness, using curvilinear and high-frequency probes.
Record patient position and the regions examined; ultrasound only shows lung that reaches the pleural surface.

checklist.label: Lung bases
checklist.detail: Look above each hemidiaphragm for consolidation with air bronchograms.

checklist.label: Pleura
checklist.detail: Assess pleural fluid, its echogenicity and lung sliding.

checklist.label: Peripheral lung lesions
checklist.detail: Look for pleural-based hypoechoic lesions that may represent infarcts in suspected pulmonary embolism.

checklist.label: Pericardium
checklist.detail: Assess pericardial fluid from the subxiphoid window and signs of tamponade.

checklist.label: Chest wall and ribs
checklist.detail: Examine the point of maximal tenderness for cortical discontinuity and haematoma.

measurements.name: Fluid depth
measurements.method: Measure the maximal perpendicular depth of pleural or pericardial fluid and state the patient position.
measurements.pitfall: Depth is not volume; report position and distribution.

measurements.name: Lesion size
measurements.method: Measure the largest dimension of a consolidation or peripheral lung lesion in two planes.
measurements.pitfall: Only the pleural-based portion of a lesion is visible.

pitfalls: A normal thoracic ultrasound does not exclude central pneumonia or central pulmonary embolism; CT pulmonary angiography remains the test for embolism.
Pleural-based hypoechoic lesions are not specific; interpret them with the clinical probability of pulmonary embolism.
impression_prompts: Is there a thoracic cause — consolidation, pleural or pericardial fluid, a peripheral lung lesion or a rib fracture — at the site of pain?
Is further imaging, such as CT pulmonary angiography or chest radiography, needed?
escalation: Immediately communicate features of cardiac tamponade or a large pericardial effusion; communicate lesions suggesting pulmonary embolism promptly.
